sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:15

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:15:1
items.html: Parts fit to look at the light: The place of bestowal, or the place of reception, of the vessel is called by the name “face.” And the bestowal or the reception itself is called by the name “a look” or “a gaze.” And this is what he says, “when the light departs from the vessel, there will be in it parts fit to look at that light” — for every departure is made by means of the refinement of the coarseness in the screen fitted in the vessel. And it is known that there are four phases in the screen; and, for example, if the phase four of the vessel was refined and the light became distant from the vessel on account of it, behold, there still remain in the vessel three phases of coarseness from which the light has not yet become distant, and they are still fit to look at the light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:15:2
items.html: The gaze of face to face becomes distant from them according to the measure of its distancing. If the coarseness was refined of phase four, behold, the light became distant from the vessel according to the measure of phase four, and not from the remaining three phases; and if it became distant also from phase three, the light will become distant from the vessel also by the measure of the coarseness of phase three, and not from the rest of the vessel, which is from phase two and above; and so forth in this way.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:15:3
items.html:
And then the vessel turned its face downward. And one must remember here all that the ARI wrote in the first expansion of Akudim in Part 4 concerning the reflected light that descends from the levels emerging at the time of the refinement and shines to the empty vessels found beneath the place of the coupling, and the matter of the striking that these illuminations make with the records remaining in those vessels (and see there in Part 4, Chapter 3, item 9, and in the Inner Light, item 50 and item 80). And from there you will understand that after the coarseness was refined, for example, from phase three to phase two — so that the coupling is made in phase two, and phase three remained empty without its own light — behold, then the reflected light descends from the illumination of the coupling of phase two into the empty vessel of phase three, and a striking and a clash is made between the descending reflected light and the record that is in the empty vessel; and the reflected light, since it now comes from the illumination of a coupling, is found to overpower the record of phase three that remained in the vessel, since the record is from the departure of the coupling. And therefore the record must go out from there and rise above the vessel in the secret of Tagin [crowns], and it gives place to the reflected light to descend into her vessel. And know that this reflected light which descended into the empty vessel acts upon the vessel so that it turns its face downward and its posterior upward, as the ARI says here.
For you know that from the aspect of the drawing of the light in the vessel, the wall of the vessel is divided and discerned into two halves, called face and posterior, or internality and externality, as the ARI says (in Part 4, Chapter 5, item 3; see there). And accordingly it is found that that empty vessel of phase three mentioned is divided into face and posterior, in which the half of its wall that is coarser is called face, it being what draws the upper light to it by means of a coupling, and the half of its wall that is not so coarse is called by the name posterior, it being quiet in the vessel, and the light having no contact with it whatever. And understand well.
And all that has been said is only at the time when the light is in the degree. However, at the time of the departure of the light from the degree of phase three to phase two — so that the coupling is made in phase two, and the illumination of this coupling descends to the empty vessel of phase three, as above — the two halves of the wall mentioned are found to turn about: its half of face becomes posterior, and its half of posterior becomes face. For the reflected light descending from phase two into the empty vessel is found to be distant from the coarseness of phase three that is there, it being a light from phase two, and it draws near to the half of the vessel's wall nearest to phase two and shines there. It follows that the coarser part of that vessel receives no illumination whatever from that reflected light and now becomes the aspect of the posterior of the vessel, and the more refined part of that vessel now becomes the face of the vessel, since the light shines only in its refined part. And this is what he says, “and then the vessel turned its face downward” — for it can receive nothing from the illumination of the coupling made in the upper phase, and the face became posterior, and it is found turning its posterior upward, since that is now what receives all of the illumination of the reflected light that descended to it; and the posterior became face. And this is called the turning about.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:15:4
items.html: That it now becomes the aspect of a vessel, etc. But afterward, when the phase above it too becomes the aspect of a vessel — that is, that the coupling departed from there as well, and the illumination of the reflected light mentioned is found to cease from descending to it — behold, then the vessel returns its face upward as at first, for its posterior has now lost all its superiority, since the record now begins to shine to the vessel, and the illumination of the record reaches only the aspect of the face of the vessel, like the light before its departure, and does not reach the aspect of its posterior. And the vessel is found restored to its place as at first.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:15:5
items.html: It looks at the upper light, etc., by way of the posterior. That is to say, that then the illumination of the coupling descending to it from the upper phase is found to be received only by way of the posterior of the vessel, which is the more refined part in it. And this is called that it turned its posterior upward. As above.
